resources.title: Peace and remembrance
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 12 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach a calm forty-minute reflection to the BUILD group of three to four. Pupils learn why some people remember, then choose a way to show care. No personal story, public answer, reading aloud or ritual is required. Keep the help route available from arrival to exit.

Outcome verbatim: Reflect on peace and remembrance (Remembrance Day). The workbook places this at BUILD Weekly - Autumn!B57/C57, originally Autumn 2 Week 5. The owner moves it to Week 2, Thursday 12 November 2026. Row B54/C54 moves to Week 5. Keep that reorder explicit; do not label C54 as the source of today’s outcome.

Theme, BUILD - Autumn!C11: Identity & Belonging. Unit, D11: Festivals & beliefs, light around the world. Term assessment, J11: F: participation and recognition.  S: festival comparison task (Dec). This lesson is formative and is a time for remembrance within the wider strand, not a celebration task.

Place Support Cards page 1, care-choice strips, word bank and the worked model at each seat. Supply books, blank slips and usual aids. Cut strips beforehand. Use learner–learner only. Display slide 3 for the starter; no public question is needed to begin.

Every task keeps a word bank, sentence starter and visible worked model. All Supported, Independent and Aspire routes retain all three. Level 2 is the requested scaffold provision, not a qualification claim. Pointing, card choice, drawing a word, usual aid and exact scribing are valid modes.

Use only the short source cards. No graphic material, war imagery, weapons, dramatic sounds, death details, reenactments or personal-loss prompts. The day is 11 November; this lesson is on 12 November, the day after. Do not imply that the observance occurs on the lesson date. People may take part in different ways or not at all.
Thursday 12 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
2 minutes private settle; 8 minutes simple care-choice starter and quiet check-ins. Words, I can __ stem and model remain on the desk.
5 minutes short source teaching with optional stretch; 5 minutes fact/choice model; 5 minutes quiet thought, care card, drawn word or scribed response.
10 minutes individual two-part record with a brief reset; 3 minutes private review and change; 2 minutes private exit.

“Remembrance Day is on 11 November. Many people remember people who died in wars. Some take time to think about peace. Today is the day after. You can think, use a card or ask me to write. You may pass. You do not need to tell a personal story.” Read calmly, one sentence at a time.

A pupil can show HELP or PASS, point or speak privately. Respond without asking for a reason in front of others. Offer the agreed quiet place within adult supervision, a brief pause, usual support, or the neutral word/shape task on Support Cards page 2. No closed eyes or silence is required. If distress continues, stop the activity and use the usual support procedure. Do not record private details in this pack.

Use “Some people think about peace” as the source-linked fact and “I can give space” as the chosen response. Privately ask the pupil to point to a source line or select a care card. If unsure, read one sentence again and offer a small choice. Do not ask for a public answer, show of hands or explanation to peers.
Thursday 12 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Supported: select one fact and one care card, then point or direct a scribe. Independent: use the source to record one fact and one chosen action in a book. Aspire: add a simple reason while recognising that others may choose differently. All routes keep the bank, stems and model. Finish is an individual source-linked fact plus a care choice, with actual help visible; a private pass is also respected and recorded honestly.

Pupil selects the fact and care choice, speaks or points to the stem. Adult records exact words or selected labels, reads back quietly, and invites keep/change. Record what the pupil chose and what the adult supplied. A copied or adult-authored statement is not independent reflection.

Cognition: one short step and small choice set. Communication: quiet wait time, usual aid, exact scribe, plan in any language. SEMH: predictable routine, calm content, no personal disclosure, private pass. Sensory/physical: large print/cards, adult cutting, no sound cue, usual equipment. Meaning uses words and position, not colour alone.

Evidence HUM-BUILD-A2-W02-E1: one fact and care choice, actual support, adult reply, NS and own response. Neutral alternative or pass is not evidence of the specific outcome unless a later response makes that link. R follows actual audience reply, NS and own response; E follows actual banking. Do not assess emotions, willingness to be silent or personal beliefs.

A helper listens to choices and treats people with care. Offer the pupil’s authentic explanation to the Communication portfolio. [AWARD] / [QUAL] mapping remains a separate staff check; no completion is inferred.

resources.title: Staff guidance and checks
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 12 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Remembrance Day is on 11 November. The lesson takes place on Thursday 12 November 2026, the day after. Use the short explanation that many people remember those who died in wars and think about peace. Do not add graphic detail or ask for personal or family experiences.

Outcome text comes from BUILD Weekly - Autumn!C57, originally Week 5. The owner moves it to taught Week 2. The original Week 2 comparison outcome at C54 moves to taught Week 5. Row C55 remains Week 3. Today’s theme is Identity & Belonging from BUILD - Autumn!C11. Spring 1’s theme is not used here.

A valid source-linked fact may be: the day is on 11 November; people remember those who died in wars; some think about peace. A care choice may be giving space, waiting for a turn, a kind word or another safe action. Pupils can select labels or direct a scribe. Do not require the model wording or a shared belief.

Date confusion: point to 11 November on S1 and say the lesson is the next day. Everyone must take part in the same way: point to choice/help/pass. Silence proves understanding: it does not; record what the pupil actually shows. A small care action ends war: avoid that claim; it is a way to show care in daily life.

Offer “Show a fact on S1” and “Choose a care card.” If needed, re-read one sentence and present two labels. No group questioning, public reading, show of hands or demand for an emotional response. Treat pass and help as valid participation choices, while leaving specific learning evidence unclaimed if absent.
Thursday 12 November 2026 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
Use learner only if a fourth pupil attends. Leave absent pupils blank. Record exact choices, actual help, adult reply, one NS and the pupil’s response on the individual form.

All tasks retain a word bank, sentence starter and visible model. The adult writes the pupil’s words or selected labels, reads back privately and checks keep/change. Record adult-supplied ideas. Do not infer independent reading or writing from a supported response.

Respond to HELP/PASS discreetly. Offer an agreed quiet space within supervision or the neutral line/dot/shape task. No personal explanation to peers or forced silence. Stop the remembrance task if needed and use the usual support procedure. A neutral task is not evidence of remembrance understanding unless the pupil later makes that link.

This is formative. Do not score personal feelings, beliefs, willingness to be silent or disclosure. R follows actual adult reply, NS and own response. E follows actual banking. Keep unfinished evidence visible. [AWARD] / [QUAL] decisions stay separate.
